fixes.explanation: Careful sounds like a good word, friend, but it isn't Paul's. He says “…open proclamation of the truth…” Open means nothing hidden, the opposite of the secret and shameful ways he just renounced. I'm careful with hot trays, but Paul's word is open.

That's right. Paul says, “The god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers, so they cannot see the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.” Picture a bakery with the ovens glowing and somebody standing there saying, "Is it dark in here?" The light is on. The blinding is what keeps them from seeing it.

Leaders sounds grand, friend, but it isn't Paul's word here. He says they are “…your servants for Jesus’ sake.” Jesus is the one he proclaims as Lord, so Paul and the people with him take the servant's spot. I'd have picked a bigger hat, but Paul went with servants.

False, friend. Paul does use the word forsaken, but he says “…persecuted, but not forsaken…” He doesn't hide the hard part, because they are persecuted. The "but not" is what makes the statement false.

Right, friend. Paul says, “For what is seen is temporary, but what is unseen is eternal.” That's his reason for fixing his eyes on what is unseen. It's like watching a cookie timer when the batch you're really waiting on is the one that lasts forever.
